set.summary: OCHA documented more than 1,800 settler attacks causing Palestinian casualties or property damage in about 280 West Bank communities in 2025, an average of five a day and the highest since it began recording in 2006. These attacks injured 1,190 Palestinians, 838 of them directly by settlers; whole herding communities were emptied, including the last six families of Khirbet Yanun near Nablus in December 2025. The UN human rights office said settler violence had forcibly displaced 2,700 Palestinians since October 2023. set.summary: After the outbreak of the Gaza war, Yemen's Houthis began firing missiles and drones at Israel and, on 19 November 2023, seized the cargo ship Galaxy Leader and its 25 crew near Hodeidah, claiming it was Israeli; Israel said neither ship nor crew were Israeli. set.summary: Israel ('Roaring Lion') and the United States ('Epic Fury') launched large-scale strikes on Iran that killed Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei and senior commanders; his son Mojtaba Khamenei succeeded him. Iran fired about 650 ballistic missiles at Israel by early April, more than half with cluster warheads, struck US bases and Gulf states, and effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz. As of 10 April 2026, according to Israeli figures reported by the Times of Israel, Iranian missiles had killed 20 civilians and foreign nationals in Israel and four Palestinians in the West Bank, more than 7,000 people in Israel had been injured (Health Ministry) and more than 5,500 Israelis displaced from damaged homes (Home Front Command); 13 US service members had been killed. In Iran, estimates quoted by Reuters put the dead at over 3,600 as of 10 April, of whom the rights group HRANA documented 1,701 civilians (the IDF claimed some 5,000 Iranian soldiers killed); UNHCR estimated about 3.2 million people temporarily displaced. A two-week US-Iran ceasefire began on 7-8 April and a Pakistan-mediated interim memorandum followed in June (14 June per CFR, 17 June per Al Jazeera), but it broke down over the Strait of Hormuz: on 8 July the US struck over 80 targets in Iran after attacks on tankers, the IRGC said it targeted US assets in neighbouring countries, and Trump said he thought the memorandum was 'over'. As of 9 October 2026 Al Jazeera described the war as in its eighth month, with talks dragging on and Trump saying he would not order a resumption of strikes before the 3 November US midterm elections.

set.summary: The United States and Iran agreed a Pakistan-mediated interim memorandum (dated 14 June by CFR; Al Jazeera says it was signed on 17 June) providing for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, an end to Hezbollah-Israel fighting in Lebanon and a 60-day cessation of hostilities while talks continued; core nuclear disputes remained unresolved. The agreement quickly broke down over control of the Strait: on 8 July the US struck over 80 targets in Iran after attacks on tankers, the IRGC said it targeted US assets in neighbouring countries, and Trump said he thought the memorandum was 'over'.
